citation: Wentworth, John. Early Chicago. Fort Dearborn: An Address Delivered at the Unveiling of the Memorial Tablet to Mark the Site of the Block-House, ... May 21st, 1881, under the Auspices of the Chicago Historical Society, to Which Have Been Added Notes and an Appendix. Fergus' Historical Series No. 16. Chicago: Fergus Printing Company, 1881.
author: John Wentworth; notes and appendix by Robert Fergus
locator: cite the printed page. pp. 31-35 the roll of officers at the post 1832-1836, with the dates each took and left command; p. 42 footnote, Matthew Burchard's report of 21 Nov 1840 naming the platted lots that hold 'Fort Dearborn within the pickets'; pp. 43-44 footnote, the fort enclosure as it stood in 1850; pp. 86-87, Gurdon S. Hubbard's letter of 20 July 1881 correcting the Wau-Bun view
note: The address Andreas points at (vol. 1, 'Late Threads of Fort Dearborn History', pp. 162-163) and never quotes. Wentworth arrived in Chicago on 25 October 1836, six weeks before the troops left, so his OWN memory is not evidence for the scene date; the value is in what he compiled around it — War Department records, the post's officer roll with dates, the surgeon's prescription book, and signed letters from men who had lived inside the fort. Tier 2 is for that compilation. Two things inside it are stronger than their container and are cited as such: Hubbard's 1881 letter is an eyewitness correction of a published picture, and the Burchard extract is a quotation from a federal land agent's report.
what_it_supplies: the command of the post through the scene date: Major John Greene from 18 Dec 1833 until 16 Sept 1835 (p. 35)
the end of the garrison: soldiers withdrawn 29 Dec 1836 under Macomb's order of 30 Nov 1836, Brevet-Major Plympton remaining in command of the post until June or July 1837 (p. 35)
the enclosure's ORIENTATION: 'nearly north and south, east and west' (Hubbard, p. 87)
the north stockade line's distance to the water in 1831: nowhere over 80 ft, and 50-60 ft opposite the north gate (Hubbard, p. 87)
the fort ground's height: 'not over eight feet above the River at its lowest stage', with the Kinzie house two or three feet higher (Hubbard, p. 87)
the north and south gates on one sight line, visible through the enclosure from the Kinzie house piazza (Hubbard, p. 87)
the platted lots covering the ground within the pickets, from Burchard's 1840 report (p. 42)
what_it_does_not_supply: a plan or any overall dimension of the 1816 stockade — no length, no width, no bastion size

the fort as it stood in 1835: the 'say 400 feet' enclosure of the pp. 43-44 footnote is the POST-ARMY compound of 1850, after the pickets had been removed and a whitewashed board fence put round it, and it is not the palisade line
any date for the removal of the pickets, which the same footnote reports only as 'at an earlier date'
